name: Returning Wave
description: Throws a wave into a box: every key opens as a bright pulse, dissolves into a haze of its own harmonics, and in its own time comes back whole.

params.name: Walls
params.description: What holds the wave. A box scatters it, a ring gathers clean overtones, a bowl swings it, two rooms add the octave under it, a fading well sinks away and rises slowly.

params.name: Reading
params.description: How the wave is heard. Density reads where it is, Wave reads its crests as a hollow tone, and Flow reads only what moves, as breath that stirs and grows still.

params.name: Width
params.description: How wide the wave is when it is thrown. A narrow wave is bright and scatters at once; a wide one is dark and slow to dissolve.

params.name: Throw
params.description: How hard the wave is thrown at the walls. More makes the opening and every return brighter and their fringes quicker, and a harder touch throws harder.

params.name: Place
params.description: Where the wave starts, from beside the wall to the middle. It combs the harmonics, and at the middle the octave comes forward.

params.name: Second
params.description: How much of a second wave is thrown against the first. The two pass through each other and leave a grain of their own.

params.name: Gap
params.description: How far from the first wave the second one starts. Near makes slow broad beating; far makes fine stripes and a brighter tone.

params.name: Return
params.description: How long until the wave is whole again. Its twelfth and its octave pass on the way; short times flicker and long ones unfold over a minute and more.

params.name: Clock
params.description: Own starts each key whole. By pitch lifts each key as its wave comes by, high keys soonest, then weaker. Shared lifts all keys on one clock, high keys a little later.

params.name: Start
params.description: Where on its way a key begins: whole, or already at the twelfth, the octave or the haze between. Turned while a key sounds it moves the wave by hand.

params.name: Freeze
params.description: Keeps time near where the key began. A little makes it swing back and forth over a long stretch; all the way nearly stops it, for one colour held.

params.name: Leak
params.description: Lets the wave leak out through the walls. Its fast parts go first, so a key darkens and dies away while it is held, from a slow fade to a pluck.

params.name: Anchor
params.description: Keeps the note's own pitch under the wave, steady while the rest dissolves and returns. At zero the pitch itself comes and goes, at the top it stands in front.

params.name: Tilt
params.description: Leans the whole spectrum, dark and round to one side, bright and open to the other.

params.name: Blur
params.description: How long a moment the ear takes in at once. Little shows every flicker; much smears quick movement away and leaves only the slow shapes.

params.name: Body
params.description: The body the wave sounds in, from a large one with a low warm ring to a small one with a high clear ring. Its resonances stay put as the keys change.

params.name: Haze
params.description: Breath that gathers on the upper harmonics as the wave dissolves and clears away when it comes back whole.

params.name: Splash
params.description: A soft burst of air where the wave is thrown, tuned to the key. A harder touch makes it louder and brighter, and it does not wait for a slow attack.

params.name: Ears
params.description: How much of the wave's own current is heard to the sides. Each key opens in the middle and widens where the wave flows, and the keys of a chord stand apart.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How long a key takes to rise. A short one lets the opening pulse be heard as a stroke; a long one lets the key appear already dissolving.

params.name: Release
params.description: How long a key takes to fade once it is let go. The wave keeps moving as it fades.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Overall output level of the instrument.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. The standing modes of a wave in a closed space are turned by their energies; the harmonics of the squared magnitude, of the wave and of its current are worked out 188 times a second and drawn into band-limited tables read at pitch. Return times, weights and levels are voiced by measurement.
